tools.name: godot_runtime_run_and_capture
tools.description:
Run the project headless (optionally a specific ``scene`` like
"res://main.tscn"), wait up to ``timeout_seconds``, then return a summary of
``errors`` / ``warnings`` / ``output`` and the exit code. Use this to verify
a change actually runs and to read back failures.

WHEN TO USE: You need to verify a scene runs without an editor open
(CI, automation, smoke test) or you want the full stdout/stderr log.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need to simulate input or inspect live state —
use play_scene() + get_game_scene_tree() / simulate_key() instead.

tools.name: godot_runtime_play_scene
tools.description:
Run the game from the editor: play ``scene_path`` (a ``res://*.tscn``) or the
project's main scene when omitted. The game connects to the editor debugger, so
runtime inspection/input tools can reach it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to interact with the running game (simulate input,
inspect live nodes, debug, test assertions).
WHEN NOT TO USE: Headless CI/automation without an editor — use
run_and_capture() instead. That runs Godot in a subprocess and returns
logs without an editor session.

IF THIS FAILS with "scene not found":
  -> The scene_path is wrong. Use get_project_info() to find the main scene,
     or get_scene_tree() to see available scenes.
IF THIS FAILS with "editor not connected":
  -> The Godot editor is not running or the addon is disabled. Check
     get_server_info() for bridge state and follow the troubleshoot prompt.

tools.name: godot_runtime_stop_scene
tools.description: Stop the current editor play session.

tools.name: godot_runtime_is_playing
tools.description: Report whether a play session is running and which scene.

tools.name: godot_runtime_get_game_scene_tree
tools.description:
Get the *running* game's live scene tree ({name, type, path, children}).
Requires an active play session with the godot-mcp runtime probe autoload; if the
probe isn't connected, returns ``connected=false`` with a ``hint`` to add it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to inspect node hierarchy, positions, or state while
the game is actively running (e.g., after simulating input to verify movement).
WHEN NOT TO USE: The editor is idle with no play session — use
get_scene_tree() to read the static scene structure instead.

tools.name: godot_runtime_capture_game_screenshot
tools.description:
Capture the *running game's* rendered viewport as a PNG image, so you can
visually verify what the player sees — including shader, lighting, and camera
output the editor viewport cannot show (the game is a separate process; the
probe grabs the frame in-process). Read-only. Requires an active play session
with the runtime probe autoload.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game (get_project_info()
     to check), then play_scene again.

tools.name: godot_runtime_get_game_output
tools.description:
Read the running game's captured output — ``print()`` lines, script
errors (with the engine's text), and warnings — as a ring of
``{seq, kind, text, time_ms}`` entries (issue #534).

Use it during a play-test to read crash traces and log-based
assertions: the capture keeps working while the game is frozen at a
debugger break (that is exactly when crash traces are readable).
``since_seq`` is an incremental cursor — pass the ``next_seq`` from
your previous call to fetch only newer entries. The ring is bounded
(500); ``dropped`` counts evicted entries honestly, so never assume
the ring holds the whole session.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game, then
     play_scene again.

tools.name: godot_runtime_monitor_property
tools.description:
Start watching ``property`` on the running game's node at ``node_path``
(an absolute path from get_game_scene_tree). The probe captures ``samples``
readings; collect them with get_property_samples. ``on_change_only`` (default)
queues a sample only when the value changed (float ``epsilon``-tolerant, also
inside Vector2/3), so a static property yields fewer deduped entries.

``runtime``: starting the monitor is a side effect on the play session.
Requires a play session + runtime probe; for a single current value use
read_property instead.

tools.name: godot_runtime_get_property_samples
godot_runtime_read_property
tools.description:
Read a property from the running game's node at ``node_path`` ONCE and
return its current value (JSON-coerced, same shapes ``monitor_property``
samples use). The dedicated #571 one-shot path: it never touches the
``monitor_property`` capture slot, so an assert or read during a running
capture cannot replace that capture's series. Requires a play session +
runtime probe.

WHEN TO USE: a single current-value check (assertions, "what is X now?").
WHEN NOT TO USE: you want a series over time — use ``monitor_property`` +
``get_property_samples``.

tools.name: godot_runtime_find_ui_elements
tools.description:
Locate live UI (Control) nodes in the running game, each with its path, class,
visibility, global ``rect`` (use it with ``simulate_mouse`` to click), and ``text``
if any. Filter by ``name_contains`` / ``class_filter`` (e.g. "Button") /
``visible_only``. Requires a play session + runtime probe.

tools.name: godot_input_simulate_key
tools.description:
Send a key event to the running game. ``key`` is a Godot key name
("A", "Space", "Enter", "Escape", …); ``pressed`` false sends a release. Optional
modifier flags (shift/ctrl/alt/meta). Requires a play session + runtime probe.
The injected event carries both keycode and physical_keycode (like real
hardware), so Input Map actions bound either way fire.

WHEN TO USE: You need to send a SINGLE key press or release (e.g., tap
Space to jump, or hold Shift for sprint). Simple, one-off interactions.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need a timed sequence of many inputs — use
play_input_sequence(events=[...], delay_ms=...) instead. That replays a
whole macro with configurable delays between events.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).

tools.name: godot_input_simulate_mouse
tools.description:
Send a mouse event at viewport position (``x``, ``y``). With ``button`` empty,
sends motion (with optional ``relative_x``/``relative_y``); with ``button`` =
left/right/middle/wheel_up/wheel_down, sends a button press/release (``pressed``).

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).

tools.name: godot_input_simulate_action
tools.description:
Press or release an input-map action (e.g. "ui_accept", "jump") on the running
game. ``strength`` (0..1) applies to a press. The action must exist in the
project's Input Map.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).
IF THIS FAILS with "unknown action":
  → The action is not in the project's Input Map. Add it via
    ProjectSettings → InputMap or use simulate_key() with the raw key name.

tools.name: godot_input_play_sequence
tools.description:
Play a sequence of input events in order, ``delay_ms`` apart. Each event is a
dict with ``type`` = "key" | "mouse" | "action" and that type's fields (as for
the simulate_* tools, e.g. ``{"type":"key","key":"Space","pressed":true}``).

WHEN TO USE: You need to replay a recorded or scripted sequence of many
inputs (e.g., a combo move, a login macro, a stress test). Events are
replayed with a fixed delay between each.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You only need a single key press — use simulate_key()
for simplicity. Or you need real-time interactive control — simulate_*
gives per-event control, while this replays a pre-built list.

tools.name: godot_input_get_stats
tools.description:
Report how many synthesized input events the running game has acknowledged —
use it to confirm injected input is reaching the game.

tools.name: godot_input_record
godot_input_stop_recording
tools.description:
Stop recording and return the captured ``events`` (in the
``play_input_sequence`` format). Polls the addon up to ``timeout_ms`` for the
buffered sequence.

``runtime`` (not read-only): it stops an active recording — a side effect on
the play session (issue #638).

tools.name: godot_debugger_set_breakpoint
tools.description:
Set a breakpoint at ``line`` in ``path`` (a ``res://`` script path).
The game must be running from the editor so the debugger session is active.

WHEN TO USE: You want the game to pause automatically when a specific
line of code is reached (e.g., to inspect state at the moment of impact).
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need the game to pause RIGHT NOW — use force_break()
instead. Setting a breakpoint only triggers when that line executes.

tools.name: godot_debugger_remove_breakpoint
tools.description: Remove a previously-set breakpoint at ``line`` in ``path``.

tools.name: godot_debugger_clear_breakpoints
tools.description: Clear every breakpoint in the current debug session (editor + game side).

tools.name: godot_debugger_force_break
tools.description:
Trigger an immediate break in the running game via the runtime probe.
Requires a play session with the godot-mcp runtime probe autoload.

WHEN TO USE: You need the game to pause RIGHT NOW so you can inspect
stack frames, step through code, or evaluate expressions (e.g., the player
just hit an enemy and you want to see local variables).
WHEN NOT TO USE: You want the game to pause later when a specific line
runs — use set_breakpoint(path, line) instead. force_break pauses
immediately, which may land in an unrelated function.

Returns ``breaked``: whether the game actually entered the break loop
(polled for up to ~2s). ``force_break_sent`` with ``breaked=False``
means the break did NOT land — do not trust stack/input tools until
``godot_runtime_is_playing`` shows ``paused=true``.

tools.name: godot_debugger_step_into
tools.description:
Step into the next line of GDScript execution. The game must be paused
(e.g. at a breakpoint or after force_break).

tools.name: godot_debugger_step_over
tools.description:
Step over the next line of GDScript execution, treating function calls
as a single step. The game must be paused.

tools.name: godot_debugger_step_out
tools.description:
Step out of the current function, pausing at the caller's next line
of GDScript execution. The game must be paused.

tools.name: godot_debugger_continue_execution
tools.description:
Resume GDScript execution after a breakpoint or forced break.
The game must be paused.

tools.name: godot_debugger_get_stack_frames
tools.description:
Get the current GDScript call stack while the game is paused.

NOT AVAILABLE on Godot 4.7 (issue #677): the paused-frame call stack is
delivered by the editor's internal ScriptEditorDebugger over the debugger
protocol, which is not exposed to editor debugger plugins — so this returns
a structured ``UNSUPPORTED`` error rather than a silent empty list.

tools.name: godot_debugger_evaluate_expression
tools.description:
Evaluate a GDScript ``expression`` in the *running game* and return its
value. Requires a play session with the runtime probe. ``error`` is set (and
``value`` null) on a parse/execute failure — never a silent null.

Issue #677: evaluation runs in-game via the probe's ``Expression`` path, so
it is evaluated in the game's global scope (base instance = the scene root);
it is **not** frame-scoped/paused-frame eval (Godot 4.7 does not expose the
paused-frame evaluator to editor debugger plugins).

Runs arbitrary code in the game process, so it is approval-gated (issue
#638): a configured approval webhook / guard must approve it first.

tools.name: godot_debugger_get_frame_variables
tools.description:
Get local, member, and global variables for the paused frame.

NOT AVAILABLE on Godot 4.7 (issue #677): paused-frame variables are served
by the editor's internal ScriptEditorDebugger, not exposed to editor debugger
plugins — this returns a structured ``UNSUPPORTED`` error.

tools.name: godot_scripts_read
tools.description:
Read the full text of the script at ``script_path`` (a ``res://`` path,
``.gd`` or ``.cs``).

tools.name: godot_scripts_list
tools.description:
List script files under ``directory`` (recursive, ``res://`` path) for a
backend: ``language="gd"`` (default) lists ``.gd``, ``"cs"`` lists ``.cs``
(C# support: issue #207 Phase 1).

Paginated: ``scripts`` is a window of ``total`` files starting at ``offset``
(default page ``limit`` 200). When ``truncated``, pass ``next_offset`` to page on.

tools.name: godot_scripts_get_for_node
tools.description:
Get the script attached to a node (by scene-relative ``node_path``, or the
selected node when omitted). ``script_path``/``content`` are null if none.

tools.name: godot_scripts_write
tools.description:
Create or overwrite the script at ``script_path`` (``res://``, ``.gd`` or
``.cs``) with ``content``. Reversible via the editor's undo. ``dry_run=True``
writes nothing and reports ``would_overwrite`` so the agent knows whether it is
about to replace an existing script. A real run reports what happened:
``created`` on a fresh file, ``overwrote``/``previous_existed`` when an existing
script was replaced.

C# (``.cs``) writes land the bytes but are NOT usable until a build — the
result carries a ``hint`` saying to validate via a C# build (Phase 2; issue
#207). GDScript is validated via ``get_parse_errors``.

tools.name: godot_scripts_patch
tools.description:
Replace every occurrence of ``find`` with ``replace`` in the script
(``.gd`` or ``.cs``). Errors if ``find`` isn't present. Reversible via undo;
``dry_run`` previews. A ``.cs`` patch still needs a C# build to take effect
(issue #207).

tools.name: godot_scripts_get_parse_errors
tools.description:
Parse-check ``script_path`` and return structured errors (message + line),
or an empty list when it parses cleanly. Use after writing/patching a script.

Scope honesty (#423): this checks GDScript *syntax* — it does NOT catch
class-API misuse (a nonexistent member parses clean and fails at runtime).
For that, run the project: ``godot_runtime_run_and_capture`` reports the
runtime errors (the recommended full-verification pattern); the shader
analogue is ``godot_shader_validate``.

Report server version and whether the Godot editor bridge is connected.

Use this first to confirm the server is up and that Godot is reachable
before issuing other commands. Also reports the connected addon's version
and flags a server↔addon version mismatch. Never mutates anything.
tools.name: godot_health_check

outputSchema.description: Server status and Godot bridge connection state.

tools.title: Godot Health Check

tools.description:
Undo the last ``count`` editor actions on the current scene's history.

With ``dry_run=True``, previews (``has_undo`` + ``would_undo_next``) without
undoing. Otherwise returns ``{undone, requested, last_action,
nothing_to_undo}``. Undoing an empty history is a no-op (``undone == 0``,
``nothing_to_undo == True``), not an error — the reversibility ledger decides
what that means.

No node/scene target to precondition — ``route()`` already surfaces a
disconnected bridge as a structured ``BRIDGE_DISCONNECTED`` error.
tools.name: godot_undo
tools.title: Godot Undo

tools.description:
Redo the last ``count`` undone editor actions on the current scene's history.

The mirror of ``godot_undo``: with ``dry_run=True``, previews (``has_redo`` +
``would_redo_next``) without redoing; otherwise returns ``{redone, requested,
last_action, nothing_to_redo}``. Redoing with nothing to redo is a no-op
(``redone == 0``, ``nothing_to_redo == True``), not an error. Use
``godot_list_history`` first when unsure which direction is available.
tools.name: godot_redo
tools.title: Godot Redo

tools.description:
Inspect the current scene's editor undo history before mutating.

Returns the version counter (increments on every committed action — a
cheap change-detector), ``has_undo`` / ``has_redo`` availability, the
current action name, the history depth, and the most recent action
names (capped, most recent last). Empty history returns zero-values,
not an error. Use it to orient before ``godot_undo`` / ``godot_redo``.
tools.name: godot_list_history

outputSchema.description:
``godot_list_history`` response: the editor history's orientation data.

``version`` increments on every committed action — a cheap change-detector
the agent can compare across calls. ``depth`` counts the history entries
(``get_history_count``, 4.4+); ``recent`` names up to 20 entries, most
recent last (``get_action_name`` indices are 0-based over the history).
``can_redo`` is the #529 ticket's field name — a documented alias of
``has_redo``, emitted so the envelope matches the issue's field list.

items.description: One editor undo-history action, named for agent orientation.

tools.title: Godot List History

tools.description:
Describe an engine class's ClassDB metadata: settable properties
(with defaults and types), methods (typed args + return), signals,
integer constants, enums, the inheritance chain, and instantiability.

Use BEFORE setting properties or calling methods by trial-and-error:
the ``type`` fields are Variant.Type names — exactly the shapes the
coercion layer accepts for ``set_node_property`` values. Engine classes
only (script ``class_name`` globals are not in ClassDB; an unknown name
returns VALIDATION_ERROR with did-you-mean suggestions). Default flags
list the class's OWN members; ``include_inherited=True`` widens every
list to the full ancestry; ``include_private=True`` keeps
``_``-prefixed entries.
tools.name: godot_describe_class
tools.title: Godot Describe Class

tools.description:

tools.description:
List the project's scene files (``res://*.tscn``) and their editor state —
which is the ``main_scene``, which are open, and which is active.

Call this to decide, when no scene is open, whether to OPEN an existing scene
(a modification / enhancement / bugfix of something already there) or CREATE a
net-new one:
  - no scenes at all -> the project is empty; godot_scene_edit_create_scene(
    root_type=…, scene_path=…) to start one (enable the scene_edit toolset first).
  - exactly one scene -> godot_scene_edit_open_scene(scene_path=that path).
  - several scenes -> open the one the request targets, or ask which to use.
Returns an empty ``scenes`` list for a project with no scenes yet (not an error).
tools.name: godot_inspection_list_scenes

outputSchema.description:
The project's scene files + which is main, for open-vs-create decisions (#304).

``scenes`` is empty for a project with no scenes yet (a net-new signal, not an error).

tools.description:
Get the open scene as a recursive tree of {name, type, path, script, children}.

Each node carries a scene-relative ``path`` (root ".") — pass it verbatim to
set_node_property / create_node(parent_path) / attach_script; never rebuild it
by hand. ``max_depth`` bounds child levels (-1 unlimited, 0 root only); a tree
over the output limit returns lightweight with ``truncated=true``. ``tree`` is
null when no scene is open. For the *running* game use get_game_scene_tree().
See docs/tool-contracts.md for ``lightweight``.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_scene_tree

outputSchema.description: The active scene tree, or ``tree=None`` when no scene is open.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Properties

tools.description:
Read a single ``property`` by name from the node at ``node_path`` — including
**built-in** Godot properties (position, scale, modulate, collision_layer,
material, theme, …) that ``get_node_properties`` omits (it returns only
script-declared variables). Returns ``{value, exists}``; ``exists=false``
(value null) when the node has no such property. The value is JSON-coerced
(Vector2 as {"x","y"}, Color, NodePath as string). Use it to snapshot a value
before ``set_node_property`` — for verification or rollback. Errors with
RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or PRECONDITION_FAILED if no
scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_node_property

outputSchema.description:
A single node property read (issue #215), including built-in Godot properties.

``value`` is JSON-coerced (see type_coerce.gd); ``exists`` is false (and ``value``
null) when the node has no such property.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Property

outputSchema.description: All property names for a node, returned by get_node_property_list.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Property List

tools.description:
List the groups the node at ``node_path`` belongs to (``{groups: [name]}``),
excluding editor-internal groups (names beginning with "_"). Use it to snapshot
membership before ``add_to_group`` / ``remove_from_group`` (or a delete) so the
change is reversible. Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve,
or PRECONDITION_FAILED if no scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_node_groups

outputSchema.description:
A node's group memberships (issue #216), editor-internal groups excluded.

Inverts ``add_to_group`` / ``remove_from_group`` and lets
``godot_scene_edit_delete_node`` restore
membership.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Groups

tools.description:
Snapshot a subtree as a stable dict (issue #535): node paths, types, script
paths, and per-node property values. Captured by default: script vars,
transforms (position/rotation/scale where the class exposes them), and group
memberships — so transform/group changes show in a diff without naming them.
``properties`` adds further built-ins by name. Returns a ``snapshot_id`` that
references the server-side store — pass it to ``diff_snapshots`` to verify a
batch mutation in one round-trip (mutate → diff → assert) instead of N
re-reads. ``max_depth`` caps depth (-1 = unlimited), like ``get_scene_tree``.
Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or
PRECONDITION_FAILED if no scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_snapshot_subtree

outputSchema.description:
A subtree snapshot (issue #535): a stable id + the serialized subtree.

``snapshot_id`` references the server-side bounded store — pass it to
``diff_snapshots`` (as ``before_id``/``after_id``) instead of re-serializing.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Snapshot Subtree

tools.description:
Diff two subtree snapshots taken with ``snapshot_subtree`` (issue #535):
``{added: [node], removed: [node], changed: [{node, property, before, after}]}``.
All three lists empty means identical. With ``after_id`` unset, the tool
re-reads the same ``node_path`` live and diffs snapshot-vs-now — the natural
acceptance check after ``batch_set_property`` / ``apply_node_edits`` /
``run_commands``. Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown/evicted id
(re-snapshot, the store is bounded).
tools.name: godot_inspection_diff_snapshots

outputSchema.description:
The diff of two subtree snapshots (issue #535).

``added``/``removed`` list node paths; ``changed`` lists per-property
before/after pairs (JSON-coerced shapes). All three empty = identical.

items.description: One property-level difference between two snapshots (issue #535).

tools.title: Godot Inspection Diff Snapshots

"res://main.tscn"), wait up to ``timeout_seconds``, then return a summary of
``errors`` / ``warnings`` / ``output`` and the exit code. Use this to verify

WHEN TO USE: You need to verify a scene runs without an editor open
(CI, automation, smoke test) or you want the full stdout/stderr log.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need to simulate input or inspect live state —
use play_scene() + get_game_scene_tree() / simulate_key() instead.

tools.title: Godot Runtime Run And Capture

tools.description:
Run the game from the editor: play ``scene_path`` (a ``res://*.tscn``) or the
project's main scene when omitted. The game connects to the editor debugger, so
runtime inspection/input tools can reach it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to interact with the running game (simulate input,
inspect live nodes, debug, test assertions).
WHEN NOT TO USE: Headless CI/automation without an editor — use
run_and_capture() instead. That runs Godot in a subprocess and returns
logs without an editor session.

IF THIS FAILS with "scene not found":
  -> The scene_path is wrong. Use get_project_info() to find the main scene,
     or get_scene_tree() to see available scenes.
IF THIS FAILS with "editor not connected":
  -> The Godot editor is not running or the addon is disabled. Check
     get_server_info() for bridge state and follow the troubleshoot prompt.

Get the *running* game's live scene tree ({name, type, path, children}).
Requires an active play session with the godot-mcp runtime probe autoload; if the
probe isn't connected, returns ``connected=false`` with a ``hint`` to add it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to inspect node hierarchy, positions, or state while
the game is actively running (e.g., after simulating input to verify movement).
WHEN NOT TO USE: The editor is idle with no play session — use
get_scene_tree() to read the static scene structure instead.
tools.name: godot_runtime_get_game_scene_tree

GameNode.description: A node in the *running* game's live scene tree (from the runtime probe).

tools.title: Godot Runtime Get Game Scene Tree

tools.description:
Capture the *running game's* rendered viewport as a PNG image, so you can
visually verify what the player sees — including shader, lighting, and camera
output the editor viewport cannot show (the game is a separate process; the
probe grabs the frame in-process). Read-only. Requires an active play session
with the runtime probe autoload.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game (get_project_info()
     to check), then play_scene again.
tools.name: godot_runtime_capture_game_screenshot
tools.title: Godot Runtime Capture Game Screenshot

tools.description:
Read the running game's captured output — ``print()`` lines, script
errors (with the engine's text), and warnings — as a ring of
``{seq, kind, text, time_ms}`` entries (issue #534).

Use it during a play-test to read crash traces and log-based
assertions: the capture keeps working while the game is frozen at a
debugger break (that is exactly when crash traces are readable).
``since_seq`` is an incremental cursor — pass the ``next_seq`` from
your previous call to fetch only newer entries. The ring is bounded
(500); ``dropped`` counts evicted entries honestly, so never assume
the ring holds the whole session.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game, then
     play_scene again.
tools.name: godot_runtime_get_game_output

outputSchema.description:
The running game's captured output ring (issue #534).

``since_seq`` filtering is applied by the addon: entries carry a monotonic
``seq`` cursor so a poll loop can pull incrementally. Honesty counts:
``dropped`` is the number of entries evicted by the bounded ring (never
silent), ``total`` the count ever captured.

items.description: One captured line from the running game's output stream (issue #534).

tools.title: Godot Runtime Get Game Output

tools.description:
Start watching ``property`` on the running game's node at ``node_path``
(an absolute path from get_game_scene_tree). The probe captures ``samples``
readings; collect them with get_property_samples. ``on_change_only`` (default)
queues a sample only when the value changed (float ``epsilon``-tolerant, also
inside Vector2/3), so a static property yields fewer deduped entries.

``runtime``: starting the monitor is a side effect on the play session.
Requires a play session + runtime probe; for a single current value use
read_property instead.
tools.name: godot_runtime_monitor_property
tools.title: Godot Runtime Monitor Property

tools.name: godot_runtime_get_property_samples
tools.title: Godot Runtime Get Property Samples

tools.description:
Read a property from the running game's node at ``node_path`` ONCE and
return its current value (JSON-coerced, same shapes ``monitor_property``
samples use). The dedicated #571 one-shot path: it never touches the
``monitor_property`` capture slot, so an assert or read during a running
capture cannot replace that capture's series. Requires a play session +
runtime probe.

WHEN TO USE: a single current-value check (assertions, "what is X now?").
WHEN NOT TO USE: you want a series over time — use ``monitor_property`` +
``get_property_samples``.
tools.name: godot_runtime_read_property

outputSchema.description:
One-shot live property read (#571): the value now, from the probe's
dedicated read path that never touches the monitor slot.

tools.title: Godot Runtime Read Property

tools.description:
Locate live UI (Control) nodes in the running game, each with its path, class,
visibility, global ``rect`` (use it with ``simulate_mouse`` to click), and ``text``
if any. Filter by ``name_contains`` / ``class_filter`` (e.g. "Button") /
``visible_only``. Requires a play session + runtime probe.
tools.name: godot_runtime_find_ui_elements
tools.title: Godot Runtime Find Ui Elements

tools.description:
Send a key event to the running game. ``key`` is a Godot key name
("A", "Space", "Enter", "Escape", …); ``pressed`` false sends a release. Optional
modifier flags (shift/ctrl/alt/meta). Requires a play session + runtime probe.
The injected event carries both keycode and physical_keycode (like real
hardware), so Input Map actions bound either way fire.

WHEN TO USE: You need to send a SINGLE key press or release (e.g., tap
Space to jump, or hold Shift for sprint). Simple, one-off interactions.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need a timed sequence of many inputs — use
play_input_sequence(events=[...], delay_ms=...) instead. That replays a
whole macro with configurable delays between events.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).
tools.name: godot_input_simulate_key
tools.title: Godot Input Simulate Key

tools.description:
Send a mouse event at viewport position (``x``, ``y``). With ``button`` empty,
sends motion (with optional ``relative_x``/``relative_y``); with ``button`` =
left/right/middle/wheel_up/wheel_down, sends a button press/release (``pressed``).

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).
tools.name: godot_input_simulate_mouse
tools.title: Godot Input Simulate Mouse

tools.description:
Press or release an input-map action (e.g. "ui_accept", "jump") on the running
game. ``strength`` (0..1) applies to a press. The action must exist in the
project's Input Map.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).
IF THIS FAILS with "unknown action":
  → The action is not in the project's Input Map. Add it via
    ProjectSettings → InputMap or use simulate_key() with the raw key name.
tools.name: godot_input_simulate_action
tools.title: Godot Input Simulate Action

tools.description:
Play a sequence of input events in order, ``delay_ms`` apart. Each event is a
dict with ``type`` = "key" | "mouse" | "action" and that type's fields (as for
the simulate_* tools, e.g. ``{"type":"key","key":"Space","pressed":true}``).

WHEN TO USE: You need to replay a recorded or scripted sequence of many
inputs (e.g., a combo move, a login macro, a stress test). Events are
replayed with a fixed delay between each.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You only need a single key press — use simulate_key()
for simplicity. Or you need real-time interactive control — simulate_*
gives per-event control, while this replays a pre-built list.
tools.name: godot_input_play_sequence
tools.title: Godot Input Play Sequence

Set a breakpoint at ``line`` in ``path`` (a ``res://`` script path).
The game must be running from the editor so the debugger session is active.

WHEN TO USE: You want the game to pause automatically when a specific
line of code is reached (e.g., to inspect state at the moment of impact).
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need the game to pause RIGHT NOW — use force_break()
instead. Setting a breakpoint only triggers when that line executes.
tools.name: godot_debugger_set_breakpoint

tools.description:
Trigger an immediate break in the running game via the runtime probe.
Requires a play session with the godot-mcp runtime probe autoload.

WHEN TO USE: You need the game to pause RIGHT NOW so you can inspect
stack frames, step through code, or evaluate expressions (e.g., the player
just hit an enemy and you want to see local variables).
WHEN NOT TO USE: You want the game to pause later when a specific line
runs — use set_breakpoint(path, line) instead. force_break pauses
immediately, which may land in an unrelated function.

Returns ``breaked``: whether the game actually entered the break loop
(polled for up to ~2s). ``force_break_sent`` with ``breaked=False``
means the break did NOT land — do not trust stack/input tools until
``godot_runtime_is_playing`` shows ``paused=true``.

tools.description:
Evaluate a GDScript ``expression`` in the *running game* and return its
value. Requires a play session with the runtime probe. ``error`` is set (and
``value`` null) on a parse/execute failure — never a silent null.

Issue #677: evaluation runs in-game via the probe's ``Expression`` path, so
it is evaluated in the game's global scope (base instance = the scene root);
it is **not** frame-scoped/paused-frame eval (Godot 4.7 does not expose the
paused-frame evaluator to editor debugger plugins).

Runs arbitrary code in the game process, so it is approval-gated (issue
#638): a configured approval webhook / guard must approve it first.
tools.name: godot_debugger_evaluate_expression

outputSchema.description:
Outcome of evaluating an expression in the running game (issue #677).

Evaluation runs in-game via the runtime probe's `Expression` path (the editor
debugger's paused-frame eval is not exposed to plugins on Godot 4.7), so it is
not frame-scoped. `error` carries a parse/execute failure message (empty on
success) — a null `value` with `evaluated=True` and an `error` is a real
failure, never a silent null.

tools.title: Godot Debugger Evaluate Expression

tools.title: Godot Scripts Get For Node

tools.description:
Create or overwrite the script at ``script_path`` (``res://``, ``.gd`` or
``.cs``) with ``content``. Reversible via the editor's undo. ``dry_run=True``
writes nothing and reports ``would_overwrite`` so the agent knows whether it is
about to replace an existing script. A real run reports what happened:
``created`` on a fresh file, ``overwrote``/``previous_existed`` when an existing
script was replaced.

C# (``.cs``) writes land the bytes but are NOT usable until a build — the
result carries a ``hint`` saying to validate via a C# build (Phase 2; issue
#207). GDScript is validated via ``get_parse_errors``.
tools.name: godot_scripts_write
tools.title: Godot Scripts Write

tools.description:
Replace every occurrence of ``find`` with ``replace`` in the script
(``.gd`` or ``.cs``). Errors if ``find`` isn't present. Reversible via undo;
``dry_run`` previews. A ``.cs`` patch still needs a C# build to take effect
(issue #207).
tools.name: godot_scripts_patch
tools.title: Godot Scripts Patch

tools.description:
Parse-check ``script_path`` and return structured errors (message + line),
or an empty list when it parses cleanly. Use after writing/patching a script.

Scope honesty (#423): this checks GDScript *syntax* — it does NOT catch
class-API misuse (a nonexistent member parses clean and fails at runtime).
For that, run the project: ``godot_runtime_run_and_capture`` reports the
runtime errors (the recommended full-verification pattern); the shader
analogue is ``godot_shader_validate``.
tools.name: godot_scripts_get_parse_errors
tools.title: Godot Scripts Get Parse Errors

tools.description:
Run a comprehensive debug check on the project and return a unified report.

This aggregates multiple diagnostics into one call so you (or the LLM) can
spot problems quickly without calling each tool individually.

Checks performed:
1. Parse errors across all GDScript files
2. Active scene tree structure (nodes, scripts, properties)
3. Headless run of the project (or a specific scene) capturing errors/warnings
4. Bridge connection state and Godot version

``scene`` — optional res:// path to focus the headless run on a specific scene.
``expected_timeout`` — set true when the game legitimately runs until killed
(sandbox/live-service games with no quit path): a timeout then means the run
behaved as designed and is not reported as a finding.
tools.name: godot_debug_workflow

outputSchema.description: Unified debug report returned by ``debug_workflow``.

tools.title: Godot Debug Workflow

tools.description:
Undo the last ``count`` editor actions on the current scene's history.

With ``dry_run=True``, previews (``has_undo`` + ``would_undo_next``) without
undoing. Otherwise returns ``{undone, requested, last_action,
nothing_to_undo}``. Undoing an empty history is a no-op (``undone == 0``,
``nothing_to_undo == True``), not an error — the reversibility ledger decides
what that means.

No node/scene target to precondition — ``route()`` already surfaces a
disconnected bridge as a structured ``BRIDGE_DISCONNECTED`` error.
tools.name: godot_undo
tools.title: Godot Undo

tools.description:
Redo the last ``count`` undone editor actions on the current scene's history.

The mirror of ``godot_undo``: with ``dry_run=True``, previews (``has_redo`` +
``would_redo_next``) without redoing; otherwise returns ``{redone, requested,
last_action, nothing_to_redo}``. Redoing with nothing to redo is a no-op
(``redone == 0``, ``nothing_to_redo == True``), not an error. Use
``godot_list_history`` first when unsure which direction is available.
tools.name: godot_redo
tools.title: Godot Redo

tools.description:
Inspect the current scene's editor undo history before mutating.

Returns the version counter (increments on every committed action — a
cheap change-detector), ``has_undo`` / ``has_redo`` availability, the
current action name, the history depth, and the most recent action
names (capped, most recent last). Empty history returns zero-values,
not an error. Use it to orient before ``godot_undo`` / ``godot_redo``.
tools.name: godot_list_history

outputSchema.description:
``godot_list_history`` response: the editor history's orientation data.

``version`` increments on every committed action — a cheap change-detector
the agent can compare across calls. ``depth`` counts the history entries
(``get_history_count``, 4.4+); ``recent`` names up to 20 entries, most
recent last (``get_action_name`` indices are 0-based over the history).
``can_redo`` is the #529 ticket's field name — a documented alias of
``has_redo``, emitted so the envelope matches the issue's field list.

items.description: One editor undo-history action, named for agent orientation.

tools.title: Godot List History

tools.description:
Describe an engine class's ClassDB metadata: settable properties
(with defaults and types), methods (typed args + return), signals,
integer constants, enums, the inheritance chain, and instantiability.

Use BEFORE setting properties or calling methods by trial-and-error:
the ``type`` fields are Variant.Type names — exactly the shapes the
coercion layer accepts for ``set_node_property`` values. Engine classes
only (script ``class_name`` globals are not in ClassDB; an unknown name
returns VALIDATION_ERROR with did-you-mean suggestions). Default flags
list the class's OWN members; ``include_inherited=True`` widens every
list to the full ancestry; ``include_private=True`` keeps
``_``-prefixed entries.
tools.name: godot_describe_class

List the project's scene files (``res://*.tscn``) and their editor state —
which is the ``main_scene``, which are open, and which is active.

Call this to decide, when no scene is open, whether to OPEN an existing scene
(a modification / enhancement / bugfix of something already there) or CREATE a
net-new one:
  - no scenes at all -> the project is empty; godot_scene_edit_create_scene(
    root_type=…, scene_path=…) to start one (enable the scene_edit toolset first).
  - exactly one scene -> godot_scene_edit_open_scene(scene_path=that path).
  - several scenes -> open the one the request targets, or ask which to use.
Returns an empty ``scenes`` list for a project with no scenes yet (not an error).

Each node carries a scene-relative ``path`` (root ".") — pass it verbatim to

by hand. ``max_depth`` bounds child levels (-1 unlimited, 0 root only); a tree
over the output limit returns lightweight with ``truncated=true``. ``tree`` is
null when no scene is open. For the *running* game use get_game_scene_tree().
See docs/tool-contracts.md for ``lightweight``.

type, attached script, exported/set properties, and child names. Errors

outputSchema.description: Full detail for a single node (path, type, script, properties, children).

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Properties

tools.description:
Read a single ``property`` by name from the node at ``node_path`` — including
**built-in** Godot properties (position, scale, modulate, collision_layer,
material, theme, …) that ``get_node_properties`` omits (it returns only
script-declared variables). Returns ``{value, exists}``; ``exists=false``
(value null) when the node has no such property. The value is JSON-coerced
(Vector2 as {"x","y"}, Color, NodePath as string). Use it to snapshot a value
before ``set_node_property`` — for verification or rollback. Errors with
RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or PRECONDITION_FAILED if no
scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_node_property

outputSchema.description:
A single node property read (issue #215), including built-in Godot properties.

``value`` is JSON-coerced (see type_coerce.gd); ``exists`` is false (and ``value``
null) when the node has no such property.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Property

tools.description:
Return the flat list of valid property names for the node at
``node_path``, plus its runtime class name. Use this to discover what
properties you can set before calling ``set_node_property``.

outputSchema.description: All property names for a node, returned by get_node_property_list.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Property List

tools.description:
List the groups the node at ``node_path`` belongs to (``{groups: [name]}``),
excluding editor-internal groups (names beginning with "_"). Use it to snapshot
membership before ``add_to_group`` / ``remove_from_group`` (or a delete) so the
change is reversible. Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve,
or PRECONDITION_FAILED if no scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_node_groups

outputSchema.description:
A node's group memberships (issue #216), editor-internal groups excluded.

Inverts ``add_to_group`` / ``remove_from_group`` and lets
``godot_scene_edit_delete_node`` restore
membership.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Groups

tools.description:
Snapshot a subtree as a stable dict (issue #535): node paths, types, script
paths, and per-node property values. Captured by default: script vars,
transforms (position/rotation/scale where the class exposes them), and group
memberships — so transform/group changes show in a diff without naming them.
``properties`` adds further built-ins by name. Returns a ``snapshot_id`` that
references the server-side store — pass it to ``diff_snapshots`` to verify a
batch mutation in one round-trip (mutate → diff → assert) instead of N
re-reads. ``max_depth`` caps depth (-1 = unlimited), like ``get_scene_tree``.
Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or
PRECONDITION_FAILED if no scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_snapshot_subtree

outputSchema.description:
A subtree snapshot (issue #535): a stable id + the serialized subtree.

``snapshot_id`` references the server-side bounded store — pass it to
``diff_snapshots`` (as ``before_id``/``after_id``) instead of re-serializing.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Snapshot Subtree

tools.description:
Diff two subtree snapshots taken with ``snapshot_subtree`` (issue #535):
``{added: [node], removed: [node], changed: [{node, property, before, after}]}``.
All three lists empty means identical. With ``after_id`` unset, the tool
re-reads the same ``node_path`` live and diffs snapshot-vs-now — the natural
acceptance check after ``batch_set_property`` / ``apply_node_edits`` /
``run_commands``. Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown/evicted id
(re-snapshot, the store is bounded).
tools.name: godot_inspection_diff_snapshots

outputSchema.description:
The diff of two subtree snapshots (issue #535).

``added``/``removed`` list node paths; ``changed`` lists per-property
before/after pairs (JSON-coerced shapes). All three empty = identical.

items.description: One property-level difference between two snapshots (issue #535).

tools.title: Godot Inspection Diff Snapshots

Read a godot:// context resource by URI — the fallback for MCP clients

"res://main.tscn"), wait up to ``timeout_seconds``, then return a summary of
``errors`` / ``warnings`` / ``output`` and the exit code. Use this to verify

WHEN TO USE: You need to verify a scene runs without an editor open
(CI, automation, smoke test) or you want the full stdout/stderr log.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need to simulate input or inspect live state —
use play_scene() + get_game_scene_tree() / simulate_key() instead.

tools.title: Godot Runtime Run And Capture

tools.description:
Run the game from the editor: play ``scene_path`` (a ``res://*.tscn``) or the
project's main scene when omitted. The game connects to the editor debugger, so
runtime inspection/input tools can reach it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to interact with the running game (simulate input,
inspect live nodes, debug, test assertions).
WHEN NOT TO USE: Headless CI/automation without an editor — use
run_and_capture() instead. That runs Godot in a subprocess and returns
logs without an editor session.

IF THIS FAILS with "scene not found":
  -> The scene_path is wrong. Use get_project_info() to find the main scene,
     or get_scene_tree() to see available scenes.
IF THIS FAILS with "editor not connected":
  -> The Godot editor is not running or the addon is disabled. Check
     get_server_info() for bridge state and follow the troubleshoot prompt.

tools.title: Godot Runtime Play Scene

tools.name: godot_runtime_stop_scene
tools.title: Godot Runtime Stop Scene

tools.title: Godot Runtime Is Playing

tools.description:
Get the *running* game's live scene tree ({name, type, path, children}).
Requires an active play session with the godot-mcp runtime probe autoload; if the
probe isn't connected, returns ``connected=false`` with a ``hint`` to add it.

WHEN TO USE: You need to inspect node hierarchy, positions, or state while
the game is actively running (e.g., after simulating input to verify movement).
WHEN NOT TO USE: The editor is idle with no play session — use
get_scene_tree() to read the static scene structure instead.
tools.name: godot_runtime_get_game_scene_tree

GameNode.description: A node in the *running* game's live scene tree (from the runtime probe).

tools.title: Godot Runtime Get Game Scene Tree

tools.description:
Capture the *running game's* rendered viewport as a PNG image, so you can
visually verify what the player sees — including shader, lighting, and camera
output the editor viewport cannot show (the game is a separate process; the
probe grabs the frame in-process). Read-only. Requires an active play session
with the runtime probe autoload.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game (get_project_info()
     to check), then play_scene again.
tools.name: godot_runtime_capture_game_screenshot
tools.title: Godot Runtime Capture Game Screenshot

tools.description:
Read the running game's captured output — ``print()`` lines, script
errors (with the engine's text), and warnings — as a ring of
``{seq, kind, text, time_ms}`` entries (issue #534).

Use it during a play-test to read crash traces and log-based
assertions: the capture keeps working while the game is frozen at a
debugger break (that is exactly when crash traces are readable).
``since_seq`` is an incremental cursor — pass the ``next_seq`` from
your previous call to fetch only newer entries. The ring is bounded
(500); ``dropped`` counts evicted entries honestly, so never assume
the ring holds the whole session.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  -> Call play_scene(scene_path) first.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe is not connected":
  -> Register MCPRuntimeProbe as an autoload in the game, then
     play_scene again.
tools.name: godot_runtime_get_game_output

outputSchema.description:
The running game's captured output ring (issue #534).

``since_seq`` filtering is applied by the addon: entries carry a monotonic
``seq`` cursor so a poll loop can pull incrementally. Honesty counts:
``dropped`` is the number of entries evicted by the bounded ring (never
silent), ``total`` the count ever captured.

items.description: One captured line from the running game's output stream (issue #534).

tools.title: Godot Runtime Get Game Output

tools.description:
Start watching ``property`` on the running game's node at ``node_path``
(an absolute path from get_game_scene_tree). The probe captures ``samples``
readings; collect them with get_property_samples. ``on_change_only`` (default)
queues a sample only when the value changed (float ``epsilon``-tolerant, also
inside Vector2/3), so a static property yields fewer deduped entries.

``runtime``: starting the monitor is a side effect on the play session.
Requires a play session + runtime probe; for a single current value use
read_property instead.
tools.name: godot_runtime_monitor_property
tools.title: Godot Runtime Monitor Property

tools.name: godot_runtime_get_property_samples
tools.title: Godot Runtime Get Property Samples

tools.description:
Read a property from the running game's node at ``node_path`` ONCE and
return its current value (JSON-coerced, same shapes ``monitor_property``
samples use). The dedicated #571 one-shot path: it never touches the
``monitor_property`` capture slot, so an assert or read during a running
capture cannot replace that capture's series. Requires a play session +
runtime probe.

WHEN TO USE: a single current-value check (assertions, "what is X now?").
WHEN NOT TO USE: you want a series over time — use ``monitor_property`` +
``get_property_samples``.
tools.name: godot_runtime_read_property

outputSchema.description:
One-shot live property read (#571): the value now, from the probe's
dedicated read path that never touches the monitor slot.

tools.title: Godot Runtime Read Property

tools.description:
Locate live UI (Control) nodes in the running game, each with its path, class,
visibility, global ``rect`` (use it with ``simulate_mouse`` to click), and ``text``
if any. Filter by ``name_contains`` / ``class_filter`` (e.g. "Button") /
``visible_only``. Requires a play session + runtime probe.
tools.name: godot_runtime_find_ui_elements
tools.title: Godot Runtime Find Ui Elements

tools.description:
Send a key event to the running game. ``key`` is a Godot key name
("A", "Space", "Enter", "Escape", …); ``pressed`` false sends a release. Optional
modifier flags (shift/ctrl/alt/meta). Requires a play session + runtime probe.
The injected event carries both keycode and physical_keycode (like real
hardware), so Input Map actions bound either way fire.

WHEN TO USE: You need to send a SINGLE key press or release (e.g., tap
Space to jump, or hold Shift for sprint). Simple, one-off interactions.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need a timed sequence of many inputs — use
play_input_sequence(events=[...], delay_ms=...) instead. That replays a
whole macro with configurable delays between events.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).
tools.name: godot_input_simulate_key
tools.title: Godot Input Simulate Key

tools.description:
Send a mouse event at viewport position (``x``, ``y``). With ``button`` empty,
sends motion (with optional ``relative_x``/``relative_y``); with ``button`` =
left/right/middle/wheel_up/wheel_down, sends a button press/release (``pressed``).

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).
tools.name: godot_input_simulate_mouse
tools.title: Godot Input Simulate Mouse

tools.description:
Press or release an input-map action (e.g. "ui_accept", "jump") on the running
game. ``strength`` (0..1) applies to a press. The action must exist in the
project's Input Map.

IF THIS FAILS with "No play session":
  → Call play_scene(scene_path) first, then retry.
IF THIS FAILS with "probe not connected":
  → Register MCPRuntimeProbe as autoload (get_project_info() to check).
IF THIS FAILS with "unknown action":
  → The action is not in the project's Input Map. Add it via
    ProjectSettings → InputMap or use simulate_key() with the raw key name.
tools.name: godot_input_simulate_action
tools.title: Godot Input Simulate Action

tools.description:
Play a sequence of input events in order, ``delay_ms`` apart. Each event is a
dict with ``type`` = "key" | "mouse" | "action" and that type's fields (as for
the simulate_* tools, e.g. ``{"type":"key","key":"Space","pressed":true}``).

WHEN TO USE: You need to replay a recorded or scripted sequence of many
inputs (e.g., a combo move, a login macro, a stress test). Events are
replayed with a fixed delay between each.
WHEN NOT TO USE: You only need a single key press — use simulate_key()
for simplicity. Or you need real-time interactive control — simulate_*
gives per-event control, while this replays a pre-built list.

tools.title: Godot Input Play Sequence

The game must be running from the editor so the debugger session is active.

WHEN TO USE: You want the game to pause automatically when a specific
line of code is reached (e.g., to inspect state at the moment of impact).
WHEN NOT TO USE: You need the game to pause RIGHT NOW — use force_break()
instead. Setting a breakpoint only triggers when that line executes.

outputSchema.description: Outcome of setting or removing a single breakpoint.

tools.description:
Trigger an immediate break in the running game via the runtime probe.
Requires a play session with the godot-mcp runtime probe autoload.

WHEN TO USE: You need the game to pause RIGHT NOW so you can inspect
stack frames, step through code, or evaluate expressions (e.g., the player
just hit an enemy and you want to see local variables).
WHEN NOT TO USE: You want the game to pause later when a specific line
runs — use set_breakpoint(path, line) instead. force_break pauses
immediately, which may land in an unrelated function.

Returns ``breaked``: whether the game actually entered the break loop
(polled for up to ~2s). ``force_break_sent`` with ``breaked=False``
means the break did NOT land — do not trust stack/input tools until
``godot_runtime_is_playing`` shows ``paused=true``.

tools.description:
Evaluate a GDScript ``expression`` in the *running game* and return its
value. Requires a play session with the runtime probe. ``error`` is set (and
``value`` null) on a parse/execute failure — never a silent null.

Issue #677: evaluation runs in-game via the probe's ``Expression`` path, so
it is evaluated in the game's global scope (base instance = the scene root);
it is **not** frame-scoped/paused-frame eval (Godot 4.7 does not expose the
paused-frame evaluator to editor debugger plugins).

Runs arbitrary code in the game process, so it is approval-gated (issue
#638): a configured approval webhook / guard must approve it first.
tools.name: godot_debugger_evaluate_expression

outputSchema.description:
Outcome of evaluating an expression in the running game (issue #677).

Evaluation runs in-game via the runtime probe's `Expression` path (the editor
debugger's paused-frame eval is not exposed to plugins on Godot 4.7), so it is
not frame-scoped. `error` carries a parse/execute failure message (empty on
success) — a null `value` with `evaluated=True` and an `error` is a real
failure, never a silent null.

result.instructions:
WARNING: You MUST follow the steps below or EVERY tool call will fail.

You are connected to a godot-mcp server that gates its tools into categories called 'toolsets'. Only 'core' (diagnostics, toolset management) and 'inspection' (read-only project/scene/node reading) are enabled by default. Every other capability is hidden until you explicitly enable it.

MANDATORY PROTOCOL — follow this order exactly:
1. Call godot_get_server_info() for a full capability snapshot (toolsets, bridge state, troubleshooting).
2. Call godot_list_toolsets() to see what is available and which are enabled — this is the authoritative enabled state, not any static claim in this text.
3. Call godot_enable_toolset(category) for every category you plan to use that godot_list_toolsets() reports as disabled. It also accepts a comma-separated list of toolsets or a bundle — author / playtest / ship — so a whole workflow is one call.
4. Only after a toolset is enabled can you call the tools in it.

WARNING: calling a gated tool whose toolset is disabled fails with "Tool '<name>' is not enabled". There is NO fallback.

QUICK DECISION TREE — what do you want to do?
- Build/edit scenes, add/move/remove nodes, change properties → scene_edit
- Write/attach GDScript, fix parse errors → scripts
- Run the game live in the editor (play, inspect, simulate input) → runtime + input
- Pause/step/inspect stack at a line → debugger + runtime
- Assert a node property meets an expectation → testing + runtime
- Apply changes to many nodes at once → batch + scene_edit
- Physics bodies, collision shapes, gravity/materials → physics + scene_edit
- Register autoloads, create custom resources → resources_edit
- Performance, bottlenecks → profiling
- Circular deps, unused resources, signal flow → analysis
- Export a build for a platform → export
- Import textures/audio/models → asset_import

Common toolsets you will need:
- scene_edit  → godot_scene_edit_create_node, godot_scene_edit_set_node_property, godot_scene_edit_attach_script, godot_scene_edit_save_scene
- scripts     → godot_scripts_write, godot_scripts_read, godot_scripts_get_parse_errors
- runtime     → godot_runtime_run_and_capture (headless), godot_runtime_play_scene (editor)
- input       → godot_input_simulate_action, godot_input_simulate_key, godot_input_play_sequence
- testing     → godot_testing_assert_node_state, godot_testing_run_test_scenario
- batch       → godot_batch_set_property, godot_batch_find_nodes_by_type
- physics     → godot_physics_setup_body, godot_physics_setup_collision
- resources_edit → godot_resources_edit_register_autoload, godot_resources_edit_create_resource
- asset_import → godot_asset_import_asset, godot_asset_import_create_material_from_textures

SERVER VS ADDON BOUNDARY:
Some tools run in the Python server (godot_list_toolsets, godot_enable_toolset, godot_get_server_info) and never message Godot. Most tools send commands to the Godot addon via a WebSocket bridge. "Tool '<name>' is not enabled" means the toolset is not enabled OR you confused a server-side tool with an addon tool — call godot_enable_toolset first.

SAFETY CONVENTION (every mutating tool):
- Mutating tools accept dry_run=True — they report what WOULD change and perform nothing. Preview first when unsure.
- Destructive tools (delete/overwrite, e.g. godot_scene_edit_delete_node, godot_scene_edit_reload_scene) require confirm=True or they refuse to run; they also support dry_run.
- Read-only tools never mutate and need neither flag.

DOCUMENTATION:
- Tutorial: https://github.com/hybridindie/godot-mcp/blob/main/TUTORIAL.md
- Tool contracts: https://github.com/hybridindie/godot-mcp/blob/main/docs/tool-contracts.md
- Architecture: https://github.com/hybridindie/godot-mcp/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

This server also exposes workflow prompts (toolset_discovery, build_scene, play_test, script_edit, debug_scene, troubleshoot) and a diagnostics tool (godot_get_server_info) that returns tool counts, bridge state, active scene, and common errors with fixes.

and flags a server↔addon version mismatch. Never mutates anything.

tools.description:
Undo the last ``count`` editor actions on the current scene's history.

With ``dry_run=True``, previews (``has_undo`` + ``would_undo_next``) without
undoing. Otherwise returns ``{undone, requested, last_action,
nothing_to_undo}``. Undoing an empty history is a no-op (``undone == 0``,
``nothing_to_undo == True``), not an error — the reversibility ledger decides
what that means.

No node/scene target to precondition — ``route()`` already surfaces a
disconnected bridge as a structured ``BRIDGE_DISCONNECTED`` error.
tools.name: godot_undo
tools.title: Godot Undo

tools.description:
Redo the last ``count`` undone editor actions on the current scene's history.

The mirror of ``godot_undo``: with ``dry_run=True``, previews (``has_redo`` +
``would_redo_next``) without redoing; otherwise returns ``{redone, requested,
last_action, nothing_to_redo}``. Redoing with nothing to redo is a no-op
(``redone == 0``, ``nothing_to_redo == True``), not an error. Use
``godot_list_history`` first when unsure which direction is available.
tools.name: godot_redo
tools.title: Godot Redo

tools.description:
Inspect the current scene's editor undo history before mutating.

Returns the version counter (increments on every committed action — a
cheap change-detector), ``has_undo`` / ``has_redo`` availability, the
current action name, the history depth, and the most recent action
names (capped, most recent last). Empty history returns zero-values,
not an error. Use it to orient before ``godot_undo`` / ``godot_redo``.
tools.name: godot_list_history

outputSchema.description:
``godot_list_history`` response: the editor history's orientation data.

``version`` increments on every committed action — a cheap change-detector
the agent can compare across calls. ``depth`` counts the history entries
(``get_history_count``, 4.4+); ``recent`` names up to 20 entries, most
recent last (``get_action_name`` indices are 0-based over the history).
``can_redo`` is the #529 ticket's field name — a documented alias of
``has_redo``, emitted so the envelope matches the issue's field list.

items.description: One editor undo-history action, named for agent orientation.

tools.description:
Describe an engine class's ClassDB metadata: settable properties
(with defaults and types), methods (typed args + return), signals,
integer constants, enums, the inheritance chain, and instantiability.

Use BEFORE setting properties or calling methods by trial-and-error:
the ``type`` fields are Variant.Type names — exactly the shapes the
coercion layer accepts for ``set_node_property`` values. Engine classes
only (script ``class_name`` globals are not in ClassDB; an unknown name
returns VALIDATION_ERROR with did-you-mean suggestions). Default flags
list the class's OWN members; ``include_inherited=True`` widens every
list to the full ancestry; ``include_private=True`` keeps
``_``-prefixed entries.
tools.name: godot_describe_class
tools.title: Godot Describe Class

(a modification / enhancement / bugfix of something already there) or CREATE a
net-new one:
  - no scenes at all -> the project is empty; godot_scene_edit_create_scene(
    root_type=…, scene_path=…) to start one (enable the scene_edit toolset first).
  - exactly one scene -> godot_scene_edit_open_scene(scene_path=that path).
  - several scenes -> open the one the request targets, or ask which to use.
Returns an empty ``scenes`` list for a project with no scenes yet (not an error).
tools.name: godot_inspection_list_scenes

outputSchema.description:
The project's scene files + which is main, for open-vs-create decisions (#304).

``scenes`` is empty for a project with no scenes yet (a net-new signal, not an error).

items.description: One project scene file and its editor state (#304).

tools.description:
Get the open scene as a recursive tree of {name, type, path, script, children}.

Each node carries a scene-relative ``path`` (root ".") — pass it verbatim to
set_node_property / create_node(parent_path) / attach_script; never rebuild it
by hand. ``max_depth`` bounds child levels (-1 unlimited, 0 root only); a tree
over the output limit returns lightweight with ``truncated=true``. ``tree`` is
null when no scene is open. For the *running* game use get_game_scene_tree().
See docs/tool-contracts.md for ``lightweight``.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_scene_tree

outputSchema.description: The active scene tree, or ``tree=None`` when no scene is open.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Scene Tree

tools.description:
Get the node currently selected in the editor — its path, type, script,
properties, and child names. Returns ``selected=None`` when nothing is
selected.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_selected_node

outputSchema.description: The selected node, or ``selected=None`` when nothing is selected.

anyOf.description: Full detail for a single node (path, type, script, properties, children).

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Selected Node

tools.description:
Get a node's detail by scene-relative path (e.g. "Player/Sprite2D"):
type, attached script, exported/set properties, and child names. Errors
with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or PRECONDITION_FAILED
if no scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_node_properties

outputSchema.description: Full detail for a single node (path, type, script, properties, children).

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Properties

tools.description:
Read a single ``property`` by name from the node at ``node_path`` — including
**built-in** Godot properties (position, scale, modulate, collision_layer,
material, theme, …) that ``get_node_properties`` omits (it returns only
script-declared variables). Returns ``{value, exists}``; ``exists=false``
(value null) when the node has no such property. The value is JSON-coerced
(Vector2 as {"x","y"}, Color, NodePath as string). Use it to snapshot a value
before ``set_node_property`` — for verification or rollback. Errors with
RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or PRECONDITION_FAILED if no
scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_node_property

outputSchema.description:
A single node property read (issue #215), including built-in Godot properties.

``value`` is JSON-coerced (see type_coerce.gd); ``exists`` is false (and ``value``
null) when the node has no such property.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Property

tools.description:
Return the flat list of valid property names for the node at
``node_path``, plus its runtime class name. Use this to discover what
properties you can set before calling ``set_node_property``.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_node_property_list

outputSchema.description: All property names for a node, returned by get_node_property_list.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Property List

tools.description:
List the groups the node at ``node_path`` belongs to (``{groups: [name]}``),
excluding editor-internal groups (names beginning with "_"). Use it to snapshot
membership before ``add_to_group`` / ``remove_from_group`` (or a delete) so the
change is reversible. Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve,
or PRECONDITION_FAILED if no scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_get_node_groups

outputSchema.description:
A node's group memberships (issue #216), editor-internal groups excluded.

Inverts ``add_to_group`` / ``remove_from_group`` and lets
``godot_scene_edit_delete_node`` restore
membership.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Get Node Groups

tools.description:
Snapshot a subtree as a stable dict (issue #535): node paths, types, script
paths, and per-node property values. Captured by default: script vars,
transforms (position/rotation/scale where the class exposes them), and group
memberships — so transform/group changes show in a diff without naming them.
``properties`` adds further built-ins by name. Returns a ``snapshot_id`` that
references the server-side store — pass it to ``diff_snapshots`` to verify a
batch mutation in one round-trip (mutate → diff → assert) instead of N
re-reads. ``max_depth`` caps depth (-1 = unlimited), like ``get_scene_tree``.
Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if the path doesn't resolve, or
PRECONDITION_FAILED if no scene is open.
tools.name: godot_inspection_snapshot_subtree

outputSchema.description:
A subtree snapshot (issue #535): a stable id + the serialized subtree.

``snapshot_id`` references the server-side bounded store — pass it to
``diff_snapshots`` (as ``before_id``/``after_id``) instead of re-serializing.

tools.title: Godot Inspection Snapshot Subtree

tools.description:
Diff two subtree snapshots taken with ``snapshot_subtree`` (issue #535):
``{added: [node], removed: [node], changed: [{node, property, before, after}]}``.
All three lists empty means identical. With ``after_id`` unset, the tool
re-reads the same ``node_path`` live and diffs snapshot-vs-now — the natural
acceptance check after ``batch_set_property`` / ``apply_node_edits`` /
``run_commands``. Errors with RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND for an unknown/evicted id
(re-snapshot, the store is bounded).
tools.name: godot_inspection_diff_snapshots

outputSchema.description:
The diff of two subtree snapshots (issue #535).

``added``/``removed`` list node paths; ``changed`` lists per-property
before/after pairs (JSON-coerced shapes). All three empty = identical.

items.description: One property-level difference between two snapshots (issue #535).

tools.title: Godot Inspection Diff Snapshots

tools.description:
Run a comprehensive debug check on the project and return a unified report.

This aggregates multiple diagnostics into one call so you (or the LLM) can
spot problems quickly without calling each tool individually.

Checks performed:
1. Parse errors across all GDScript files
2. Active scene tree structure (nodes, scripts, properties)
3. Headless run of the project (or a specific scene) capturing errors/warnings
4. Bridge connection state and Godot version

``scene`` — optional res:// path to focus the headless run on a specific scene.
``expected_timeout`` — set true when the game legitimately runs until killed
(sandbox/live-service games with no quit path): a timeout then means the run
behaved as designed and is not reported as a finding.
tools.name: godot_debug_workflow

outputSchema.description: Unified debug report returned by ``debug_workflow``.

tools.title: Godot Debug Workflow
